name: chill-to-the-bone-low-phantasia-debuff
notes: Branch A (0-1 phantasias controlled by the caster), now exercising the card's actual primary use case: the DEFENDING player (player 2) casts Chill to the Bone on the ATTACKING player's (player 1's) attacking ally, mid-combat. Previously this fixture had the attacker cast the spell on their own attacking ally to avoid a real engine bug: ChillToTheBoneResolve() (GameLogic.php) read the DecisionQueueController 'CombatAttacker' variable -- a raw 'myField-N' mzID string stored from the ATTACKER's own perspective (see StoreCombatAttackerState) -- and called GetZoneObject($attackerMZ) directly on it, without first calling ConvertMzToPlayerPerspective($attackerMZ, $attackerPlayer) the way AtmosShieldRedirect/InterceptTargetChosen (CombatLogic.php) do for the exact same situation. When the DEFENDER (a different player than $playerID) cast the spell, GetZoneObject('myField-1') resolved against the caster's own (empty) field slot instead of the attacker's field, and the effect silently no-opped. That bug has now been fixed: ChillToTheBoneResolve() reads 'CombatAttackerPlayer' (falling back to GetTurnPlayer() if unset, matching the convention used elsewhere in this file, e.g. IsUnitAttacking()/IsUnitDefending() in GameLogic.php) and calls ConvertMzToPlayerPerspective($attackerMZ, $attackerPlayer) before GetZoneObject(), so the lookup resolves correctly regardless of which player is casting the spell relative to who's attacking. Verified live (via a scripted probe using DevTools/TestAutomationBridge.php) that reverting the fix causes this exact action sequence to leave the attacker's TurnEffects empty (silent no-op), and that with the fix applied TurnEffects gets the expected 'p00ghqhcpb-2' tag. Setup seeds player 1 with an awake Dungeon Guide directly onto myField-1 (bypassing the turn-1 summoning-sickness/attack-lock by advancing to global turn 2 via two decline cycles, matching the existing project convention for real-attack fixtures such as ardent-cloudstriker-west-attack-champion-buff) and seeds Chill to the Bone directly into player 2's hand (both players otherwise run a Dungeon Guide/Fluffy Shopkeep-only deck with a Spirit of Water starting champion, since Chill to the Bone is WATER-element and needs that lineage unlocked). Because player 2 holds a Speed=true card the whole game, every phase transition before the real attack (end of turn 1, the turn-2 materialize offer, and the recollection-phase window it chains into) independently opens its own fast-opportunity window that player 2 must explicitly decline -- confirmed empirically -- before the real post-attack-declaration window (with CombatAttacker/CombatAttackerPlayer genuinely live) is taken for real. Dungeon Guide's printed POWER 1 / LIFE 3 becomes -1 / 1 after the -2/-2 debuff.

rulesClauses: Target attacking ally gets -2 POWER and -2 LIFE until end of turn.
If you control two or more phantasias, that ally gets -4 POWER and -4 LIFE instead. (0-1 phantasia branch only -- see chill-to-the-bone-two-phantasia-debuff for the other branch)
Perspective-correctness: the effect resolves correctly when cast by the DEFENDING player (a different player than the attacker), not just when the attacker casts it on their own ally.
